culture: Fort Lauderdale's expectation culture runs coastal and sun-soaked. Beach-town energy in the New River district, a dense network of OB practices on Atlantic and Las Ollas, and a large Latin community — Spanish-language birth resources genuinely matter here, and many local doulas and midwives work bilingually. Families delivering in the area typically land at one of the big Broward Health campuses, with Holy Cross Fort Lauderdale close behind. If you're planning a hospital birth, an out-of-hospital-style birth plan plus a doula who knows the L&D team is the combination that makes the difference.
heroLocalDetail: New River's bridges at golden hour, with the Fort Lauderdale skyline just a short drive away. Doulas in this area know every L&D unit in Broward County by name — and the coffee shops where they debrief after long shifts.
medicaidNote: Florida Medicaid (Family Plus/CHIP) covers doula services for eligible members — FL was one of the earlier states to add doulas to its Medicaid provider directory. Call 1-800-342-3526 (Access Florida) or check your plan to confirm current coverage before booking. If you're on a commercial plan, many FL plans cover part of the doula package — worth one call to the number on your card.
insuranceNote: Whether your FL plan covers doula services depends on the carrier — Aetna, Humana, Cigna and local plans all differ, and some cover doulas with a physician referral. Call the member-services number on your insurance card and ask specifically: 'Does my plan cover doula services with a referral?' If it does, get the authorization number in writing before your birth.
